facts.text: Oak Ridge earned its nickname “Secret City” during World II when the Manhattan Project’s Y‑12 and X‑10 plants were built in secrecy.
The Oak Ridge National Laboratory, now a leading research hub, began as the X‑10 graphite reactor, the first full‑scale plutonium production plant.
The Oak Ridge Room at the public library houses a vast collection of Manhattan Project photographs and biographies of key scientists.
The Manhattan Project National Historical Park in Oak Ridge preserves the town’s wartime legacy and is managed jointly by the National Park Service and the Department of Energy.
Oak Ridge’s early infrastructure boasted 300 miles of roads, 55 miles of railroad, ten schools, and seven theaters, built to support the wartime workforce.
